page: Amazon Web Services i7ie.24xlarge is a storage-optimized server built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8559C processors delivering 48 physical cores and 96 vCPUs running at a baseline frequency of 3.2 GHz, supported by 320 MB of L3 cache. It incorporates 768 GB of DDR5 system memory operating at 6 GHz, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio. Persistent high-throughput storage is provisioned via 60,000 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD space, coupled with a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. The system does not include dedicated graphics processing units, but it integrates Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction support for specialized compute tasks.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate strong multi-threaded compute capability, highlighted by a Geekbench multi-core score of 21,420.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 93,157.6, both positioning within the top ten percent of tested instances. The memory subsystem recorded 287.5 GB/sec in large-block uncached read operations, facilitating high-speed data access. Operational tests reflect high data-handling throughput, registering 109.38 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 128.24 GB/sec in static web serving throughput. PassMark database operations and multi-threaded decompression tests similarly place in the top quartile.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the platform integrates dense NVMe storage directly with high-capacity system memory, eliminating external storage protocol overhead for latency-sensitive environments. Single-core performance occupies the middle tier of benchmark distributions, indicating that raw single-threaded execution is traded for high I/O throughput and aggregate compute capacity. The server fits high-capacity transactional databases, distributed NoSQL datastores, real-time analytics engines, in-memory caching clusters, and large-scale data ingest pipelines.
